chunks: And it was said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A man takes the Hajj-payment from another man, then he dies and leaves nothing behind.” So he said:
“It suffices for the deceased, and if he had a Hajj with Allah, it will be recorded for its owner.”

key_terms.الْحَجَّةَ: the payment or commission for performing Hajj on behalf of another
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person on whose behalf the legal effect is considered
key_terms.لِصَاحِبِهِ: for its owner, meaning the one who provided it

ai.seo_question: If someone accepts money for Hajj and then dies leaving nothing, does the Hajj still count for the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning funds given for Hajj when the recipient dies before leaving any estate behind. The Imam عليه السلام states that the Hajj counts on behalf of the deceased, and if a Hajj was already established for him with Allah, the reward is recorded for the one who provided the payment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2871 - It was said to Abu Abdullah (as): "A man takes funds for Hajj from someone, but he dies and leaves nothing behind."
Imam (as) said: "It suffices for the deceased, and if he had a Hajj recorded with Allah (swt), it will be credited to the one who provided the funds."
